```{r co-gates}
chk_stop("Cohort is not empty", nrow(cohort) > 0)

chk_stop("Every cohort student is in the entry grade in the entry year",
         all(cohort$D_stu_id %in% entrants$D_stu_id))

chk_stop("Every cohort student has a school attribution",
         !any(is.na(cohort$C_cohort_school_id)))

chk_stop("Cohort schools are all in scope",
         all(cohort$C_cohort_school_id %in% included_location_ids),
         offenders = cohort |>
           filter(!C_cohort_school_id %in% included_location_ids) |>
           count(C_cohort_school_id, C_cohort_school_name, name = "n_students"))

chk_info("Overall cohort retention against the Tettra snapshot benchmark",
         paste0(round(100 * nrow(cohort) / funnel$start, 1), "% vs ",
                config$cohort$benchmarks$snapshot_retention_pct, "% benchmark"))
```

# Stage 7 — Course coding join

The rollup the old pipeline never actually built. `02` sized the mismatch
between transcript and catalogue but never joined them, so no analysis could
cut by ERS subject, rigor or credit type.

Stage 3.6 established that exact matching on course ID **plus** name reaches
99.99% of rows, so the primary join is exact and the fallback handles a
residue of about 125 rows.

## 7.1 Prepare the coded file

```{r cd-prepare}
chk_stage("Stage 7 — Course coding join")

chk_stop("Coding file is available", !is.null(course_coding_raw),
         detail = "Stage 1 could not read it; see the Stage 1 log")

coding <- course_coding_raw |>
  rename(any_of(unlist(config$column_map$course_coding))) |>
  rename_with(~ sub("^c_", "C_", .x), starts_with("c_"))

chk_info("Coded fields available", ncol(coding),
         data = tibble(column = names(coding)))

missing_fields <- setdiff(config$coding_join$required_coded_fields, names(coding))
chk_stop("Required coded fields present",
         length(missing_fields) == 0,
         detail = if (length(missing_fields) > 0)
           paste("Missing:", paste(missing_fields, collapse = ", ")))
```

The join key must be unique in the coded file or the join multiplies transcript
rows. `join_checked` would catch that, but catching it here names the problem
more clearly.

```{r cd-key-unique}
chk_unique(coding, config$coding_join$keys,
           "Coded file is unique on course ID + name")
```

## 7.2 Primary join

```{r cd-join}
transcript_coded <- transcript_student |>
  join_checked(coding, by = config$coding_join$keys,
               check = "Course coding onto transcript",
               report_unmatched = TRUE)

chk_rows_stable(transcript_student, transcript_coded,
                "Coding join did not change the transcript row count")

transcript_coded <- transcript_coded |>
  mutate(C_coding_source = if_else(
    is.na(C_course_subject_area), NA_character_, "id_and_name"))

chk_info("Rows coded on the primary key",
         paste0(format(sum(!is.na(transcript_coded$C_course_subject_area)),
                       big.mark = ","), " (",
                round(100 * mean(!is.na(transcript_coded$C_course_subject_area)), 3), "%)"))
```

## 7.3 Fallback on course ID

Only where a course ID maps to exactly one coded course. `BUS3718S1` answers to
four different names in the transcript, so an unconditional ID fallback would
hand it whichever coding happened to come first.

```{r cd-fallback}
if (config$coding_join$fallback == "id_when_unambiguous") {

  unambiguous <- coding |>
    group_by(D_course_id) |>
    filter(n_distinct(C_course_id) == 1) |>
    slice(1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(-D_course_name)

  chk_info("Course IDs mapping to exactly one coded course",
           paste0(format(nrow(unambiguous), big.mark = ","), " of ",
                  format(n_distinct(coding$D_course_id), big.mark = ",")))

  coded_cols <- setdiff(names(unambiguous), "D_course_id")

  filled <- transcript_coded |>
    filter(is.na(C_course_subject_area)) |>
    select(-all_of(coded_cols), -C_coding_source) |>
    inner_join(unambiguous, by = "D_course_id") |>
    mutate(C_coding_source = "id_only")

  chk_info("Rows recovered by the ID fallback", nrow(filled),
           data = filled |> count(D_course_id, D_course_name, name = "n_rows") |>
             arrange(desc(n_rows)) |> head(20))

  transcript_coded <- bind_rows(
    transcript_coded |> filter(!is.na(C_course_subject_area) |
                                        !D_course_id %in% filled$D_course_id),
    filled) |>
    distinct(D_stu_id, D_year, D_course_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

  chk_rows_stable(transcript_student, transcript_coded,
                  "Fallback did not change the transcript row count")
}
```

```{r cd-coverage}
transcript_coded |>
  count(C_coding_source, name = "rows") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * rows / sum(rows), 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(rows))
```

```{r cd-uncoded}
uncoded <- transcript_coded |>
  filter(is.na(C_course_subject_area))

chk_info("Rows still uncoded", nrow(uncoded),
         data = uncoded |> count(D_course_id, D_course_name, name = "n_rows") |>
           arrange(desc(n_rows)))
```

## 7.4 What the coding gives us

The first look at the transcript through ERS categories rather than district
course names.

```{r cd-subject-area}
transcript_coded |>
  filter(!is.na(C_course_subject_area)) |>
  group_by(C_course_subject_area) |>
  summarise(rows = n(),
                   students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
                   creds_earned = round(sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(rows))
```

```{r cd-rigor}
transcript_coded |>
  filter(!is.na(C_course_rigor)) |>
  count(C_course_rigor, C_course_rigor_detail, name = "rows") |>
  arrange(desc(rows))
```

The EPSO, work-based learning and industry-credential flags are the fields the
Arnold hypotheses turn on, so it is worth seeing their scale now.

```{r cd-epso}
transcript_coded |>
  filter(!is.na(C_course_subject_area)) |>
  group_by(D_year) |>
  summarise(
    rows          = n(),
    pct_epso      = round(100 * mean(C_course_epso_flag, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    pct_wbl       = round(100 * mean(C_course_wbl_flag, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    pct_ic        = round(100 * mean(C_course_ic_flag, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop")
```

```{r cd-epso-type}
transcript_coded |>
  filter(!is.na(C_course_epso_type)) |>
  count(C_course_epso_type, name = "rows") |>
  arrange(desc(rows))
```

## 7.5 Coverage where it matters

Overall coverage can look excellent while a specific population is poorly
covered. The cohort is the population every headline number will be built on.

```{r cd-coverage-cohort}
transcript_coded |>
  mutate(in_cohort = D_stu_id %in% cohort$D_stu_id) |>
  group_by(in_cohort) |>
  summarise(rows = n(),
                   pct_coded = round(100 * mean(!is.na(C_course_subject_area)), 3),
                   .groups = "drop")
```

```{r cd-coverage-year}
  group_by(D_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(),
                   pct_coded = round(100 * mean(!is.na(C_course_subject_area)), 3),
                   .groups = "drop")
```

```{r cd-gates}
chk_stop("Course coding match rate",
```

# Stage 8 — Output and check report

One table carries everything: the coded transcript at student x year x course,
with the analysis fields and both selection flags attached. The snapshot export
is a filtered copy of that same table rather than a separately built object, so
the two cannot drift apart.

## 8.1 Analysis fields

The legacy `04_transcript_analysis` recomputed these on every run. Computing
them once, here, with checks, means every analysis starts from the same
definitions.

```{r out-analysis-fields}
chk_stage("Stage 8 — Output")

bucket_grade <- function(x, buckets) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  for (b in buckets) {
    hit <- is.na(out) & !is.na(x) & x >= b$min
    out[hit] <- b$label
  }
  out
}

transcript_out <- transcript_coded |>
  mutate(
    C_course_failed    = !is.na(D_creds_possible) & D_creds_possible > 0 &
                          !is.na(D_creds_earn) & D_creds_earn == 0,
    C_grade_pct_rollup = bucket_grade(D_stu_grade,
                                      config$analysis_fields$grade_pct_buckets),
    C_course_marked_repeat = C_course_name_starred
  )

chk_info("Failed course rows",
         paste0(format(sum(transcript_out$C_course_failed), big.mark = ","), " (",
                round(100 * mean(transcript_out$C_course_failed), 1), "%)"))

transcript_out |>
  count(C_grade_pct_rollup, name = "rows") |>
  arrange(desc(rows))
```

### Credit recovery

A later-term row earning more credit than it attempted, where the same
student's earlier-term row for the same base course earned zero. No hardcoded
passing mark.

```{r out-credit-recovery}
earlier_failed <- transcript_out |>
  filter(C_term == "Semester 1") |>
  distinct(D_stu_id, D_year, C_course_id_base, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(D_stu_id, D_year, C_course_id_base,
                   s1_failed = !is.na(D_creds_earn) & D_creds_earn == 0)

transcript_out <- transcript_out |>
  left_join(earlier_failed,
                   by = c("D_stu_id", "D_year", "C_course_id_base")) |>
  mutate(
    C_credit_recovery_flag = coalesce(
      C_creds_earn_exceeds_attempted & C_term == "Semester 2" & s1_failed, FALSE)) |>
  select(-s1_failed)

chk_info("Credit recovery rows",
         paste0(format(sum(transcript_out$C_credit_recovery_flag), big.mark = ","),
                " across ",
                format(n_distinct(
                  transcript_out$D_stu_id[transcript_out$C_credit_recovery_flag]),
                  big.mark = ","), " students"))

transcript_out |>
  filter(C_credit_recovery_flag) |>
  count(D_year, name = "rows")
```

### Mobility

`04` built `C_pure_cohort` from two transfer flags. Both are derivable from
what Stage 5 already computed.

```{r out-mobility}
mobility <- student_year |>
  arrange(D_stu_id, D_year) |>
  group_by(D_stu_id) |>
  mutate(prev_school = lag(C_home_school_id)) |>
  summarise(
    C_transferred_within_year  = any(n_schools > 1),
    C_transferred_across_years = any(!is.na(prev_school) &
                                       prev_school != C_home_school_id),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(C_pure_cohort = !C_transferred_within_year &
                                !C_transferred_across_years)

chk_info("Students who never changed school", 
         paste0(format(sum(mobility$C_pure_cohort), big.mark = ","), " (",
                round(100 * mean(mobility$C_pure_cohort), 1), "%)"))

transcript_out <- transcript_out |>
  join_checked(mobility, by = "D_stu_id", check = "Mobility flags onto transcript")
```

## 8.2 Selection flags

```{r out-selection-flags}
# C_stu_cohort and C_stu_snapshot use Tettra's field names and its
# include/exclude values, so anyone working from the guidance finds what they
# expect. The logical twins exist because "include" does not sum.
transcript_out <- transcript_out |>
  mutate(
    C_cohort_include = D_stu_id %in% cohort$D_stu_id,
    C_stu_cohort     = if_else(C_cohort_include, "include", "exclude"),
    C_eoy_grade      = C_stu_grade_level)

chk_info("Transcript rows belonging to cohort students",
         paste0(format(sum(transcript_out$C_cohort_include), big.mark = ","), " (",
                round(100 * mean(transcript_out$C_cohort_include), 1), "%)"))
```

## 8.3 Snapshot selection

Independent of the cohort: a single-year population, selected on its own
criteria. Set `snapshot$enabled: false` for a cohort-only project.

```{r out-snapshot}
if (isTRUE(config$snapshot$enabled)) {

  snap_year <- config$snapshot$year
  snap_base <- student_year |> filter(D_year == snap_year)

  chk_info(paste0("Snapshot ", snap_year, " — students enrolled"), nrow(snap_base))

  snap_funnel <- funnel_new(snap_base$D_stu_id,
                            paste0("Enrolled in ", snap_year))

  snap_funnel <- funnel_add(snap_funnel, "Grade level in range",
    snap_base$D_stu_id[snap_base$C_stu_grade_level %in% config$snapshot$grade_levels])

  if (isTRUE(config$snapshot$require_school_in_scope)) {
    snap_funnel <- funnel_add(snap_funnel, "Home school in scope",
      snap_base$D_stu_id[snap_base$C_home_school_in_scope])
  }

  # The legacy script summed days without group_by, so every student received
  # the same total and the flag was uniform. Grouping is what makes this a
  # per-student test.
  if (config$snapshot$duration_basis == "credits_attempted") {
    creds <- transcript_out |>
      filter(D_year == snap_year) |>
      group_by(D_stu_id) |>
      summarise(creds_attempted = sum(D_creds_possible, na.rm = TRUE),
                       .groups = "drop")
    snap_funnel <- funnel_add(snap_funnel,
      paste0("Attempted >= ", config$snapshot$credits_attempted_min, " credits"),
      creds$D_stu_id[creds$creds_attempted >= config$snapshot$credits_attempted_min])
  } else {
    thr <- if (config$snapshot$duration_basis == "share")
      config$snapshot$duration_min_share * window_days else config$snapshot$duration_min_days
    snap_funnel <- funnel_add(snap_funnel,
      paste0("Enrolled >= ", round(thr), " days"),
      snap_base$D_stu_id[snap_base$M_days_enrolled_year >= thr])
  }

  snapshot_ids <- snap_funnel$ids
  chk_info("Snapshot selected", length(snapshot_ids),
           detail = paste0(round(100 * length(snapshot_ids) / snap_funnel$start, 1),
                           "% of students enrolled in ", snap_year))
} else {
  snapshot_ids <- character(0)
  chk_info("Snapshot", "disabled in config")
}
```

```{r out-snapshot-funnel}
if (isTRUE(config$snapshot$enabled)) {
  funnel_report(snap_funnel, config$cohort$benchmarks$snapshot_retention_pct)
}
```

```{r out-snapshot-flag}
transcript_out <- transcript_out |>
  mutate(
    C_stu_snapshot_include = D_stu_id %in% snapshot_ids &
                             D_year == config$snapshot$year,
    C_stu_snapshot = if_else(C_stu_snapshot_include, "include", "exclude"))

chk_info("Transcript rows in the snapshot",
         format(sum(transcript_out$C_stu_snapshot_include), big.mark = ","))
```

## 8.4 Final table

Columns ordered by prefix so the table reads consistently across districts:
`D_` district-reported, `C_` ERS-created, `M_` measures.

```{r out-order}
transcript_out <- transcript_out |>
  select(starts_with("D_"),
                starts_with("C_"),
                starts_with("M_"),
                everything())

chk_unique(transcript_out, c("D_stu_id", "D_year", "D_course_id"),
           "Output is one row per student / year / course")

chk_rows_stable(transcript_coded, transcript_out,
                "Stage 8 added columns without changing rows")

chk_info("Output shape",
         paste0(format(nrow(transcript_out), big.mark = ","), " rows x ",
                ncol(transcript_out), " cols"))

tibble(column = names(transcript_out),
               type   = map_chr(transcript_out, ~ class(.x)[1]),
               pct_missing = map_dbl(transcript_out,
                                            ~ round(100 * mean(is.na(.x)), 1)))
```

## 8.5 Scope the export

Everything above ran on the full transcript, because the diagnostics are only
meaningful against the whole file. What leaves the pipeline is a different
question, and config decides it.

Filtering to the cohort does more than shrink the file. A cohort student is
enrolled in every required year by definition, so the orphan rows — coursework
transferred in from before a student enrolled — disappear along with their
missing home school and missing demographics. Every row in the export is fully
populated.

```{r out-scope}
rows_rule <- config$outputs$coded_transcript$rows

keep <- switch(rows_rule,
  all                = rep(TRUE, nrow(transcript_out)),
  cohort_only        = transcript_out$C_cohort_include,
  cohort_or_snapshot = transcript_out$C_cohort_include |
                       transcript_out$C_stu_snapshot_include,
  stop("Unknown outputs$coded_transcript$rows: ", rows_rule, call. = FALSE))

if (isTRUE(config$outputs$coded_transcript$restrict_to_cohort_years)) {
  keep <- keep & transcript_out$D_year %in% cohort_years
}

transcript_export <- transcript_out |> filter(keep)

chk_info("Export row rule", rows_rule)
chk_info("Rows exported",
         paste0(format(nrow(transcript_export), big.mark = ","), " of ",
                format(nrow(transcript_out), big.mark = ","), " (",
                round(100 * nrow(transcript_export) / nrow(transcript_out), 1), "%)"))
chk_info("Students exported", n_distinct(transcript_export$D_stu_id))
```

The export should be complete on every field that was patchy in the full file.
If it is not, a student got into the cohort who should not have.

```{r out-export-completeness}
tibble(
  measure = c("Rows", "Students", "Years",
              "% with a home school", "% coded", "% with an enrolment record"),
  value = c(
    format(nrow(transcript_export), big.mark = ","),
    format(n_distinct(transcript_export$D_stu_id), big.mark = ","),
    paste(sort(unique(transcript_export$D_year)), collapse = ", "),
    paste0(round(100 * mean(!is.na(transcript_export$C_home_school_id)), 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(100 * mean(!is.na(transcript_export$C_course_subject_area)), 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(100 * mean(transcript_export$C_has_enrolment_record), 2), "%")))
```

```{r out-export-by-year}
transcript_export |>
  group_by(D_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(),
                   students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
                   median_courses = round(n() / n_distinct(D_stu_id), 1),
                   creds_earned = round(sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
                   .groups = "drop")
```

```{r out-export-gates}
chk_stop("Export is not empty", nrow(transcript_export) > 0)

if (rows_rule == "cohort_only") {
  chk_stop("Every exported student is in the cohort",
           all(transcript_export$D_stu_id %in% cohort$D_stu_id))

  # Completeness only follows when the export is confined to the cohort years.
  # A district supplying more years than the cohort spans can legitimately give
  # a cohort student pre-enrolment coursework, and that is not a failure.
  n_no_school <- sum(is.na(transcript_export$C_home_school_id))
  if (isTRUE(config$outputs$coded_transcript$restrict_to_cohort_years) ||
      all(unique(transcript_export$D_year) %in% cohort_years)) {
    chk_stop("Every exported row has a home school", n_no_school == 0,
             detail = "within the cohort years a cohort student is enrolled every year",
             offenders = transcript_export |>
               filter(is.na(C_home_school_id)) |>
               count(D_stu_id, D_year, name = "n_rows"))
  } else {
    chk_info("Exported rows outside the cohort years with no home school",
             n_no_school,
             detail = "pre-enrolment coursework for cohort students; expected")
  }
}

chk_unique(transcript_export, c("D_stu_id", "D_year", "D_course_id"),
           "Export is one row per student / year / course")
```

## 8.6 The student-year export

Tettra keeps every student and distinguishes with a flag, and asks that the
cohort be tested for comprehensiveness against the full 9th-grade population.
A cohort-only transcript cannot answer that, so the denominator lives here
instead — every student-year, with every criterion outcome and the reason each
excluded student dropped out.

Narrow and short enough that keeping everyone costs nothing.

```{r out-student-year}
student_year_export <- student_year |>
  left_join(cohort_criteria, by = "D_stu_id") |>
  left_join(mobility, by = "D_stu_id") |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(D_stu_id, C_cohort_school_id,
                                           C_cohort_school_name),
                   by = "D_stu_id") |>
  mutate(
    C_stu_cohort   = coalesce(C_stu_cohort, "exclude"),
    C_stu_snapshot = if_else(D_stu_id %in% snapshot_ids &
                                      D_year == config$snapshot$year,
                                    "include", "exclude"),
    C_entry_cohort_candidate = D_stu_id %in% entrants$D_stu_id)

chk_unique(student_year_export, c("D_stu_id", "D_year"),
           "Student-year export is one row per student per year")

chk_info("Student-year export",
         paste0(format(nrow(student_year_export), big.mark = ","), " rows x ",
                ncol(student_year_export), " cols"))

student_year_export |>
  filter(C_entry_cohort_candidate, D_year == config$cohort$entry_year) |>
  count(C_stu_cohort, C_cohort_exclusion_reason, name = "students") |>
  arrange(desc(students))
```

## 8.7 Write

The snapshot is filtered from the same full table rather than from the export,
so a snapshot student who is not in the cohort is still written out.
## 8.7 Write to SharePoint

Nothing is written locally. `put()` reports each file into the check log, so
the run report records exactly what left the pipeline and how big it was.

```{r out-write}
out_folder <- config$raw_data_folder_path
out_prefix <- config$outputs$subfolder %||% "/"

put <- function(data, name) {
  if (is.null(data) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    chk_info(paste0("Output SKIPPED (empty): ", name), 0)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  path <- paste0(out_prefix, name)
  ers_write_sharepoint(data                     = data,
                       folder_path              = out_folder,
                       file_name_with_extension = path)
  chk_info(paste0("Output written: ", name),
           paste0(format(nrow(data), big.mark = ","), " rows x ",
                  ncol(data), " cols"),
           detail = paste0(out_folder, path))
  invisible(data)
}

if (isTRUE(config$outputs$coded_transcript$write)) {
  put(transcript_export, config$outputs$coded_transcript$file_name)
}

if (isTRUE(config$outputs$student_year$write)) {
  put(student_year_export, config$outputs$student_year$file_name)
}

if (isTRUE(config$snapshot$enabled) && isTRUE(config$outputs$snapshot$write)) {
  put(transcript_out |> dplyr::filter(C_stu_snapshot_include),
      config$outputs$snapshot$file_name)
}
```
